images.caption: Fig. 1:The idea ofATEST. Standard test-time scaling (TTS) generates the same number of samples for a query whether the GPU is idle or busy.ATESTlooks at the live GPU load. When the GPU is busy and each sample costs more energy, it skips samples that are not worth their cost.

Fig. 2:Overview ofATEST. (a) Standard TTS generates a fixed number of samplesBBand does not use the live GPU state. (b)ATEST-Calibrated, the offline mode ofATEST, builds accuracy and cost models offline for each dataset and picksBBonce per query. (c)ATEST-Online starts with one sample and adds samples step by step (→→→→81\!\to\!3\!\to\!4\!\to\!6\!\to\!8). (d) An illustration of one decision: \scriptsize1⃝ a Monte Carlo look-ahead toBmax=8B_{\max}=8estimates how likely the current winner is to stay the winner, andΔ​U\Delta Uis how much the next step raises this; \scriptsize2⃝ the online cost model learns from the measured energy of every step, follows the load, and predicts the next step’s energy with a safety margin; \scriptsize3⃝ with the same votes,ATEST-Online continues on an idle GPU but stops on a busy one.

Fig. 3:Motivation. (a) Energy per answered query for a fixed budget ofB=4B=4at four GPU load levels, relative to idle. The value under each level is the measured GPU utilization. (b) Error of the offline cost model, averaged over four datasets. Without live GPU state (Adaptive-Cal), the error grows from 26% at idle to 283% at high load. Adding live GPU state (ATEST-Calibrated) lowers the high-load error to 55%, but the error is still large at medium load (130%).

Fig. 4:Behavior at each load level (125 queries per level). Top: accuracy over all queries (deferred = wrong). Middle: deferred queries (%). Bottom: meanBBoveransweredqueries.ATEST-Online (blue, solid) never defers and lowers its budget as load rises.ATEST-Calibrated (orange, dashed) also lowers its budget, but it starts deferring at medium or high load on all four datasets, which pulls its accuracy down.
